ticket: R6 of plans/aws_redeployment_tickets.md (KMS key: the runtime role decrypts through the key policy)
supersedes: aws-redeployment-od6-stack-layout-r3_2026-10-22, decision OD6-r3-parameters, the kms stack's parameter list only: AdminRoleArn is no longer a kms parameter (R6-D4); it stays a secret-stack parameter. authority: Agent-authored under CLAUDE.md, recording decisions the operator gave in session on 2026-10-26 on the agent's R6 proposals. Execution aid for infrastructure work (CLAUDE.md section 10.2). Closes no gate, adds no runtime gate, dispatches no phase, touches no Tier 1-3 source and amends no constitutional rule.
decided_by: the operator, in session on 2026-10-26 ('1-9 a (a 4b-vel egyutt)', ~16:31 UTC), accepting option (a) of each of the nine points and of point 4b, and stating that the 1 USD/month key fee is the 'free (key: monthly)' case of OD6-r3. Point 10 (CloudTrail decrypt and the S3 Bucket Key, added by the agent after F-R6-4) answered '10a' (~16:44 UTC).
decision: The KMS stack (deploy/aws/templates/30-kms.yaml) creates one customer-managed symmetric single-Region key with yearly rotation, retained on stack deletion and replacement, and the alias alias/${ProjectName}. Its key policy has five statements and four principals: the account root (kms:*, IAM delegation), the runtime role imported from the IAM stack (kms:Decrypt and kms:DescribeKey only via Secrets Manager or S3 in this Region), CloudTrail for the project trail (GenerateDataKey* and DescribeKey, by aws:SourceArn and the CloudTrail encryption context) and CloudWatch Logs in this Region for the /${ProjectName}/ log groups. The stack exports KeyArn, KeyId and KeyAliasName.
why: The ticket: the runtime role decrypts through the key policy, not through an IAM side grant (F1 closed for KMS); every service grant is scoped as the service's own guide prescribes; nothing administers the key except through IAM under the root delegation.
inputs: plans/aws_redeployment_handoff_2026-10-21.md section 4 (F1), section 5 (OD2, OD8, OD11), sections 6, 7 and 7a
docs/infrastructure_security/evidence/04_kms/kms_key_policy.json and CG4_steps.txt, as history only (old account, us-east-1, bedrock role that no process used)

AWS documentation read 2026-10-26: CloudFormation reference AWS::KMS::Key; CloudTrail user guide 'Configure AWS KMS key policies for CloudTrail'; CloudWatch Logs user guide 'Encrypt log data in CloudWatch Logs using AWS KMS'; Secrets Manager user guide 'Secret encryption and decryption'; IAM user guide 'Testing IAM policies with the IAM policy simulator' and 'IAM policy simulator: how to'; AWS KMS pricing page (read 2026-10-25, R6 handoff)

findings.finding: Before R6, eu-north-1 holds two KMS keys, both AWS-managed (the RDS and Lambda default keys) and enabled, no customer-managed key, twelve alias/aws/* aliases and no alias/proposal-orchestrator; the stack proposal-orchestrator-kms does not exist (exit 254); no trail is visible in eu-north-1, organization shadow trails included, so the name proposal-orchestrator-bedrock-trail is free.

The seven proposal-orchestrator-iam-* exports exist; proposal-orchestrator-iam-RuntimeRoleArn = arn:aws:iam::797661577394:role/proposal-orchestrator-runtime-role, equal to R5_outputs.json. The runtime role holds exactly the four R5 managed policies and no inline policy, so no identity policy grants it kms:Decrypt before R6.

AWS::KMS::Key: KeySpec default SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT, KeyUsage default ENCRYPT_DECRYPT, MultiRegion default false; RotationPeriodInDays 90-2560, default 365; PendingWindowInDays 7-30, default 30; changing KeySpec, KeyUsage, Origin or MultiRegion fails the update regardless of UpdateReplacePolicy; removing the key from a stack schedules its deletion, which the template cannot cancel; every key-policy principal must exist; the key takes Tags; Ref returns the key id, GetAtt Arn the ARN. AWS::KMS::Alias takes no Tags and is already in UNTAGGABLE_TYPES, so the template guard is unchanged.

CloudTrail requires kms:GenerateDataKey* (conditioned by aws:SourceArn = the trail ARN and kms:EncryptionContext:aws:cloudtrail:arn like the account's trails) and kms:DescribeKey (aws:SourceArn). Its guide also lists a decrypt grant for the CloudTrail service principal and states that kms:Decrypt is required to create or update a trail with SSE-KMS when the trail's existing S3 bucket uses an S3 Bucket Key.
findings.basis: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html, read 2026-10-26. v1 history: the v1 key policy granted CloudTrail only GenerateDataKey* and DescribeKey and the v1 trail was created and delivered (evidence/04_kms/kms_key_policy.json, evidence/06_cloudtrail).

findings.finding: CloudWatch Logs: the principal is logs.<Region>.amazonaws.com in the key's own Region; actions kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:GenerateDataKey*, kms:Describe*; the guide's account-wide variant conditions kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn with ArnLike. R6 narrows it to log-group:/${ProjectName}/*.

AWS's own Secrets Manager key-policy example conditions kms:Decrypt and kms:DescribeKey with kms:ViaService = secretsmanager.<Region>.amazonaws.com; GetSecretValue makes Secrets Manager call kms:Decrypt on the caller's behalf. No code under runner/, deploy/*.sh, deploy/*.json or scripts/ calls KMS directly (grep, 2026-10-26).
The IAM policy simulator documentation names resource-based policy simulation for S3 buckets, SQS queues, SNS topics and Glacier vaults (console) and does not mention KMS keys.

decisions.question: Key cost (handoff section 4, point 1)
decisions.answer: Proceed. The key costs 1 USD/month prorated hourly, plus 1 USD/month for each of the first two rotations (about 3 USD/month from the second year), paid from credits. The operator states this is the 'free (key: monthly)' case of OD6-r3, not an hourly-billed resource of the kind R11 gates.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer in session ('1 usd az OD6-r3 free (key: monthly) esete').
decisions.consequence: STEPS.md states the monthly fee in its header. R14's cost check counts the key.

decisions.question: Trail name (point 2)
decisions.answer: Lasting rule: the trail is ${ProjectName}-bedrock-trail (register v2 DC-23), ARN arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudtrail:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:trail/${ProjectName}-bedrock-trail, home Region eu-north-1.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '2a'. The key policy must name the trail before it exists.
decisions.consequence: R7 creates exactly that trail, in eu-north-1. A different name or home Region needs a successor record and an UPDATE of the key policy first.

decisions.question: kms:ViaService on the runtime role's grant (point 3)
decisions.answer: The runtime role's kms:Decrypt and kms:DescribeKey carry StringEquals kms:ViaService in [secretsmanager.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com, s3.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com].
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '3a'. The host never calls KMS directly (F-R6-6); R8's secret and R7's deploy bucket reach the key through those two services.
decisions.consequence: A direct SDK call (e.g. DescribeKey) by the runtime role is refused. R8 and R11 show the grant works; a refusal there leads to a successor record and an UPDATE change set.

decisions.question: An admin statement for AdminRoleArn (point 4 and 4b)
decisions.answer: No admin statement: the account-root kms:* statement is the only administrative grant; the admin role (OD11-r2) administers the key through its AdministratorAccess. AdminRoleArn leaves 30-kms.yaml, parameters/kms.json, the kms case of tests/test_aws_iac_contract.py::test_admin_role_is_the_r1_role_arn_with_its_path and the README table's kms entry. 4b: recorded here as superseding OD6-r3-parameters for the kms stack only.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '4a' and '4b a'. DC-19 ('root, the runtime role, CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs only') then holds literally.

decisions.question: Retention and deletion (point 5)
decisions.answer: DeletionPolicy Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy Retain on the key; PendingWindowInDays 30.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '5a'. Deleting or replacing the stack must never schedule the deletion of the key that encrypts the trail, the logs, the secret and the deploy bundles.
decisions.consequence: The kms stack is not deleted: deleting it would leave the key (and its fee) and remove the alias, and recreating it would create a second key. Retiring the key is a manual ScheduleKeyDeletion with a successor record.

decisions.question: Rotation period (point 6)
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '6a'. The default, pinned by the test and visible in get-key-rotation-status.
decisions.consequence: DC-18 is evidenced with KeyRotationEnabled true and RotationPeriodInDays 365.

decisions.question: Guard and tests (point 7)
decisions.answer: tests/test_aws_kms_template.py pins the stack's shape: key and alias only; symmetric, single-Region, enabled, rotation 365; Retain policies and a 30-day window; tags; the five key-policy statements exactly; principals root, the runtime role through Fn::ImportValue only, CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs; kms:Decrypt only for the runtime role, CloudWatch Logs and (through kms:*) root; kms:* only for root; no Principal '*'; alias alias/${ProjectName}; no AdminRoleArn; outputs equal the contract. The template guard is unchanged (F-R6-3).
decisions.consequence: deploy/aws/README.md lists the KMS template test with the others.

decisions.question: How 'no IAM policy grants that role Decrypt separately' is evidenced (point 8)
decisions.answer: The runtime role's attached and inline policies, read after the stack exists, equal R6_03 and R5_08; one simulate-principal-policy of kms:Decrypt on the new KeyArn with aws:RequestedRegion = eu-north-1 and no resource policy returns implicitDeny with AllowedByOrganizations and AllowedByPermissionsBoundary true; get-key-policy shows the key-policy grant, compared statement by statement with the template by script. No key-policy simulation (F-R6-7).
decisions.consequence: The grant itself is exercised by R8 (secret read) and R11 (host).

decisions.question: Register v2 statuses (point 9)
decisions.answer: On a PASS verification: DC-18 VERIFIED_PASS; DC-19 VERIFIED_PASS on the policy-level criterion, noted 'CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs grants exercised in R7, runtime grant in R8/R11'.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '9a'; same pattern as R5-D9 for DC-10.
decisions.consequence: R7, R8 and R11 report any refusal against DC-19.

decisions.question: CloudTrail kms:Decrypt and the S3 Bucket Key (point 10, added by the agent after F-R6-4)
decisions.answer: Lasting rule: the key policy grants CloudTrail no kms:Decrypt. R7 creates the trail bucket without an S3 Bucket Key on this CMK (BucketKeyEnabled false or unset), so the CloudTrail guide's decrypt requirement for Bucket-Key buckets does not arise.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '10a'. CloudTrail only encrypts with this key; the v1 trail was created and delivered without a CloudTrail decrypt grant (F-R6-4). The narrowest grant that works.
decisions.consequence: R7's audit template and its test pin the trail bucket's encryption without an S3 Bucket Key. If R7 shows that trail creation needs CloudTrail decrypt anyway, R7 stops and a successor record adds the statement by UPDATE change set.

known_gaps.gap: That the trail is created and delivers without a CloudTrail decrypt grant when the bucket has no S3 Bucket Key is shown by R7 (v1 history supports it).
That Secrets Manager and S3 are the only paths by which the runtime role needs the key is shown by R8 and R11's live calls.

The AWS-managed organization's RCPs, which can apply to KMS, are not visible from the member account (OD11-r2 known gap). A restriction would show as an explicit deny at the change set (R6), or at first use (R7, R8).

not_evidence_of: Any KMS resource in account 797661577394: this record precedes the first R6 change set.
That CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs or the runtime role can use the key in practice (R7, R8, R11).
